deed: מבצע שלמה העלה 14,325 מיהודי אתיופיה לישראל בתוך 36 שעות
title: Operation Solomon: Within 36 hours, Israel brought more than 14,000 Ethiopian Jews to Israel

trailer.text: Operation Solomon was the third aliyah operation from Ethiopia to Israel, after Operation Moses in 1984 and Operation Joshua in 1985.
According to the Jewish Agency, in 1991 Ethiopia was embroiled in a civil war, and rebel forces were advancing toward Addis Ababa and the Jews there.
According to the Jewish Agency, on May 24–25, 1991, more than 14,300 Ethiopian Jews were secretly brought from Addis Ababa to Israel, within 36 hours.
According to JDC, Israeli planes made 40 continuous flights that weekend.
According to the Jewish Agency, a few days after the operation was completed, Addis Ababa fell to the rebels.

glance.label: Who
glance.value: The Government of Israel and the Jewish Agency

paragraphs.text: According to the Jewish Agency, in 1991 Ethiopia was embroiled in a decades-long civil war and was facing a famine.
According to the Agency, rebel forces were advancing toward Addis Ababa and toward the Jews there, and this caused grave concern among the Israeli and American-Jewish agencies on the ground.
According to the JDC Archives, there was fear that Ethiopian Jews would be caught in the crossfire.

According to Israel National News, citing the official IDF blog, Ethiopia had prohibited its Jews from immigrating to Israel, and because of this, in the 1970s Israel authorized the IDF to act to bring the Jews of Ethiopia to Israel.
According to the Jewish Press, the ruler Mengistu was willing to discuss the Jews' emigration only in exchange for weapons.

According to the Jerusalem Post, in 1989 Israel and Ethiopia renewed their relations after 16 years of separation, and from then on several hundred Jews immigrated each month in a family reunification program.
According to JDC, the organization ran health and welfare programs for the Ethiopian Jews who had gathered in Addis Ababa.
According to The Jewish Chronicle, Operation Moses in the mid-1980s secretly rescued some 8,000 Ethiopian Jews.

stations.title: The secret planning and the letter from Washington

paragraphs.text: According to Ono Academic College, in 1991 the regime of Mengistu Haile Mariam was about to collapse, and Israel saw this as an unparalleled opportunity to bring the remaining Beta Israel.
According to the same source, Israel, under the leadership of Prime Minister Yitzchak Shamir, had already begun in 1990 to plan covertly to bring as many Ethiopian Jews as possible.
According to JNS, Avi Mizrahi, then 38, was sent to Ethiopia in September 1990 to set the stage for the operation.
According to Ono Academic College, Susan Pollack, director of the AAEJ in Addis Ababa, stressed the urgency of the operation and drew support from the U.S. government.
According to Jewish Press, President Bush sent Senator Rudy Boschwitz as a special emissary to meet with the Ethiopian government, to aid Israel in arranging the airlift.
According to Ono Academic College, on May 22, 1991, Bush sent a letter to the President of Ethiopia, and the agreement was reached the next day.
According to the Jewish Agency and the Jewish Press, the agreement of May 23 allowed the Jews to leave Ethiopia all at once, following Bush's letter to the new President, Tesfaye Gebre Kidan.
According to Israel Hayom, American Jewry raised $35 million within a few hours, to cover the payment demanded by the Ethiopian government.
Israel National News also reports that the Jewish community raised the sum almost immediately.
According to the Jerusalem Post, the Ethiopian government received the money in exchange for safe passage, with the assistance of donations from diaspora Jews, mainly Americans.
According to Ono Academic College, the donation of American Jews enabled the operation to begin.
According to the Jewish Agency, it and the Government of Israel were the main players in planning and executing the operation.

According to JNS, alongside the Jewish Agency, JDC, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Mossad and the IDF, the North American federations and the American Association for Ethiopian Jews also assisted.
According to JDC, the organization helped to negotiate and plan the rescue.

According to Israel Hayom, in the weeks before the operation, the Jewish Agency and JDC oversaw the identification of the Jews eligible to make aliyah and the issuing of documents, so that family members would stay together.
According to JNS, because of weight limits, the immigrants were instructed to leave their belongings at home, except for a few Judaica items.
According to Israel National News, the Jews gathered at the Israeli embassy, and from there were bused to the planes.
According to JDC, the organization provided food and fuel and coordinated transportation to the planes, together with the Israeli embassy.
According to the Jerusalem Post, Avi Mizrahi was in charge of airport operations in Ethiopia for the Jewish Agency.
Mizrahi told JNS that nobody pushed to be first in line, and that he did not hear a single child cry, even though there were many children there.
According to Israel Hayom, on May 24–25, 1991, 14,325 Ethiopian Jews were brought from Addis Ababa to Israel, on continuous flights by 35 Israeli aircraft.
According to the Jewish Press, the operation was not publicized by the media because of a gag order under military censorship.
According to JNS, the Air Force and El Al stripped the planes of seats to fit in as many passengers as possible.
According to Israel National News, the Air Force deployed no fewer than six Boeing 707 planes and 18 Hercules planes.
According to the Jerusalem Post, hundreds of IDF soldiers in civilian clothing helped carry out the operation and transported the masses from Addis Ababa to Ben Gurion Airport.
According to Israel National News, Maj. Gen. Avihu Bin-Nun was then commander of the Air Force, and Benny Gantz, later Chief of Staff, led the ground operation as commander of the Shaldag unit.
According to the JDC Archives, a 10-to-15-day evacuation was originally planned, and it was later cut down to 48 hours.
According to JDC, the operation was in fact completed in just 36 hours.

stations.title: One plane, more than a thousand passengers

paragraphs.text: According to Transportation History, an El Al Boeing 747 flew out of Ethiopia on May 24 with 1,122 passengers on board.
According to the Israel Forever Foundation, this flight set a world record for the number of passengers on a single flight.
According to the Jewish Agency, all the seats were removed, and at least 1,078 people were on board one plane.
According to the Jewish Agency, the passengers on this plane included two babies born in-flight.
According to the Jewish Press, five pregnant women gave birth on the plane, and they and their babies were taken to the hospital immediately upon landing in Israel.
According to Israel National News, when the first plane landed in Israel, Prime Minister Yitzhak Shamir and other leaders greeted the immigrants.
Mizrahi told JNS that when the immigrants landed in Israel, they immediately kissed the ground.
According to the Jewish Press, 140 frail passengers received medical care while still on the tarmac.
According to the Jewish Agency, a few days after the end of the operation, Addis Ababa fell to the rebels.
According to JNS and those involved in it, Operation Solomon was the largest and most complex aliyah operation up to that time.
According to the Jerusalem Post, the operation has since been deemed a major humanitarian success.
In 2021, on the thirtieth anniversary of the operation, Jewish Agency CEO Amira Ahronoviz said that it is a reminder that all of the Jewish people are responsible for one another.
According to Israel Hayom, for more than 40 years the Jewish Agency and the Government of Israel have assisted more than 95,000 Ethiopian Jews to immigrate to Israel.
According to JNS, Racheli Tadesa Malkai immigrated in Operation Solomon at age 8.
According to JNS, upon arriving in Israel she was asked to change her Ethiopian name, Amevet, to the name she goes by today.
Malkai told JNS that the older generation had a more difficult time adjusting to life in Israel.
According to JNS, some thirty years after the operation, she runs a nonprofit organization that empowers Ethiopian women.

disagreements.question: How many Ethiopian Jews were brought in the operation?

versions.says: Jewish Press and Israel National News: 14,500

disagreements.question: How many planes took part in the operation?

versions.says: JDC: 34 Israeli planes, which made 40 flights

disagreements.question: How many passengers were on the most crowded plane?

versions.says: Transportation History and Israel Forever Foundation: 1,122 passengers on an El Al 747
The Jewish Agency: at least 1,078 people
According to Ono Academic College, one of the aircraft carried 1,008 people, and it says this is an unbroken world record for the largest number of passengers on a single flight.

disagreements.question: How many babies were born during the flights?

versions.says: The Jewish Agency: two babies on one plane
The Jewish Chronicle: up to seven babies
Jewish Press: five women gave birth on the plane

disagreements.question: How long did the operation last?

versions.says: The Jewish Agency, JDC and Israel National News: 36 hours
JDC Archives: the operation was done by midday Saturday
Avi Mizrahi, in a 2021 interview: within 24 hours

claims.text: לפי ישראל היום, מבצע שלמה היה מבצע העלייה השלישי מאתיופיה לישראל, אחרי מבצע משה ב-1984 ומבצע יהושע ב-1985.
claims.quote: Operation Solomon was the third aliyah mission from Ethiopia to Israel. It was preceded by Operation Moses in 1984 and Operation Joshua in 1985.

claims.text: לפי הסוכנות היהודית, ב-1991 אתיופיה הייתה שקועה במלחמת אזרחים בת עשורים ועמדה בפני רעב.
claims.quote: In 1991, Ethiopia had been embroiled in a decades-long civil war and was facing a famine.

claims.text: לפי הסוכנות היהודית, כוחות המורדים התקדמו לעבר אדיס אבבה והיהודים שם, מה שעורר דאגה רבה בקרב הגופים הישראליים והיהודיים-אמריקאיים בשטח.
claims.quote: Rebel forces were advancing toward Addis Ababa and the Jews there, causing grave concern among Israeli and American-Jewish agencies on the ground in Ethiopia.

claims.text: לפי הסוכנות היהודית, בתוך 36 שעות ב-24–25 במאי 1991 הועלו בחשאי מאדיס אבבה לישראל יותר מ-14,300 יהודי אתיופיה.
claims.quote: Within 36 hours on May 24-25, 1991, more than 14,300 Ethiopian Jews were covertly airlifted from Addis Ababa to Israel during Operation Solomon

claims.text: לפי הג'וינט (JDC), באותו סוף שבוע 34 מטוסים ישראליים ביצעו 40 טיסות רצופות, ובסך הכול הגיעו לישראל קצת יותר מ-14,000 יהודי אתיופיה.
claims.quote: That weekend, 34 Israeli planes made 40 continuous flights, and just over 14,000 Ethiopian Jews were brought to safety in Israel

claims.text: לפי הסוכנות היהודית, המבצע החל למחרת ההסכם, וימים ספורים לאחר שהסתיים נפלה אדיס אבבה בידי המורדים.
claims.quote: Operation Solomon started the next day and a few days after the Operation was completed, Addis Ababa fell to the rebels.

claims.text: לפי הסוכנות היהודית, הסוכנות וממשלת ישראל היו הגורמים המרכזיים בתכנון המבצע וביצועו.
claims.quote: The Jewish Agency along with the Government of Israel were the main players in planning and executing Operation Solomon

claims.text: לפי ישראל היום, המבצע החשאי התקיים ב-24–25 במאי 1991: 14,325 יהודי אתיופיה הועלו מאדיס אבבה לישראל בטיסות רצופות של 35 כלי טיס ישראליים.
claims.quote: The covert military operation took place on May 24-25, 1991, when 14,325 Ethiopian Jews were airlifted from Addis Ababa to Israel on nonstop flights involving 35 Israeli aircraft

claims.text: לפי הג'וינט, מבצע שתוכנן להימשך 48 שעות הושלם ב-36 שעות בלבד.
claims.quote: In the end, what was designed to take 48 hours was completed in just 36

claims.text: לפי ישראל היום, יהדות ארה"ב התגייסה וגייסה 35 מיליון דולר תוך שעות ספורות כדי לשלם את התשלום שדרשה ממשלת אתיופיה.
claims.quote: American Jewry mobilized in support of the operation, raising $35 million in just a few hours to cover the payment demanded by the Ethiopian government.

claims.text: לפי הקריה האקדמית אונו, יהודים אמריקאים תרמו 35 מיליון דולר ותרמו רבות למאמץ הכספי והציבורי, וכך אפשרו את תחילת המבצע.
claims.quote: American Jews contributed greatly to the financial and advocacy efforts, donating $35 million to the cause, enabling Operation Solomon to begin.

claims.text: לפי ארכיון הג'וינט, היה חשש שההתקוממות תיצור מצב מסוכן שבו יהודי אתיופיה ייתפסו בקרב אש צולבת.
claims.quote: There was also fear that the unrest could create a dangerous situation, with Ethiopian Jews being caught in the crossfire.

claims.text: לפי Israel National News, אתיופיה אסרה על יהודיה לעלות לישראל.
claims.quote: Ethiopia had prohibited its Jews from making aliyah (immigration) to Israel

claims.text: לפי תוכנית לימודים של הקריה האקדמית אונו, ב-1991 שלטונו של מנגיסטו היילה מריאם עמד לקרוס, וישראל זיהתה בכך הזדמנות חסרת תקדים להביא את שארית בני בטא ישראל.
claims.quote: Israel recognized that this transition offered an unparalleled opportunity to bring the remaining Beta Israel from Ethiopia.

claims.quote: Up to that point, Mengistu was only willing to discuss their emigration in exchange for weapons.

claims.quote: Israel and Ethiopia renewed diplomatic ties in 1989 after 16 years of separation, which allowed several hundred Jews to immigrate to Israel monthly in a family reunification program

claims.quote: JDC helped to negotiate and plan the rescue, which came on the heels of comprehensive health and welfare programs

claims.quote: Operation Solomon, which followed the Operation Moses rescue of some 8,000 Ethiopian Jews in secret in the mid-1980s, was an ambitious and daring plan.

claims.text: לפי הקריה האקדמית אונו, בהנהגת ראש הממשלה יצחק שמיר ישראל החלה כבר ב-1990 בתכנון חשאי להעלות כמה שיותר יהודי אתיופיה.
claims.quote: Under the leadership of Prime Minister Yitzchak Shamir, Israel had already begun its covert plans in 1990, aiming to airlift as many Ethiopian Jews as possible.

claims.text: לפי JNS, אבי מזרחי, בן 38, נשלח לאתיופיה בספטמבר 1990 כדי להכין את הקרקע למבצע שנערך כשישה חודשים אחר כך.
claims.quote: A year earlier, in September of 1990, the 38-year-old was sent to Ethiopia to help set the stage for the mission that would take place six months later.

claims.text: לפי הקריה האקדמית אונו, סוזן פולק, מנהלת AAEJ באדיס אבבה, פעלה להדגיש את דחיפות המבצע וגייסה תמיכה של ממשלת ארה"ב.
claims.quote: The director of the AAEJ in Addis Ababa, Susan Pollack, intervened to stress the urgency of the mission, drawing support from the U.S. government.

claims.text: לפי Jewish Press, הנשיא בוש שלח את הסנאטור רודי בושוויץ כשליח מיוחד לפגישה עם ממשלת אתיופיה כדי לסייע לישראל בארגון מבצע האוויר.
claims.quote: U.S. Senator Rudy Boschwitz was sent as a special emissary by Pres. Bush to meet with the Ethiopian government to aid Israel in arranging the airlift.

claims.quote: U.S. President George Bush sent a letter to Acting President of Ethiopia Tesfaye Gebre-Kida on May 22, 1991, and an agreement was reached the very next day, on May 23.

claims.text: לפי הסוכנות היהודית, לאחר שהנשיא ג'ורג' בוש האב שלח מכתב לנשיא אתיופיה החדש טספיי גבר קידאן, הושג ב-23 במאי הסכם שאפשר ליהודים לצאת מאתיופיה בבת אחת.
claims.quote: After President George H.W. Bush sent a letter to the new Ethiopian President, Tesfaye Gebre Kidan, an agreement was reached on May 23, allowing Jews to leave Ethiopia all at once.

claims.text: לפי Jewish Press, ממשלת אתיופיה התירה סוף סוף לכל היהודים לצאת בבת אחת, במידה רבה בזכות מכתב מנשיא ארה"ב ג'ורג' בוש האב.
claims.quote: The Ethiopian government finally allowed all the Jews to leave the country at once in great part due to a letter from U.S. President George H.W. Bush.

claims.text: לפי Israel National News, הקהילה היהודית גייסה כמעט מיד 35 מיליון דולר כדי לשלם לממשלת אתיופיה תמורת היתר ליהודים לצאת.

claims.quote: The local government was paid roughly $35 million, with the assistance of donations from the diaspora Jewish community, namely Americans, to secure their safe passage.

claims.quote: In cooperation with the Israeli embassy, JDC provided food and fuel, coordinated transportation to the planes, and more.

claims.quote: says former shaliach (emissary) Avi Mizrahi, who at the time of Operation Solomon was in charge of Ethiopian airport operations for The Jewish Agency

claims.quote: Nobody pushed or shoved to be first in line; I never heard a single child cry, even though there were many of them.

claims.quote: The operation itself was not publicized by media, thanks to a gag order under military censorship.

claims.text: לפי Jewish Press, חמש נשים הרות ילדו במטוס, והן ויילודיהן הועברו לבית החולים מיד עם הגעתן לישראל.
claims.quote: five pregnant women gave birth on the plane

claims.text: לפי Israel National News, כשהמטוס הראשון נחת בישראל קיבלו את פני העולים ראש הממשלה יצחק שמיר ומנהיגים נוספים.
claims.quote: As the first plane landed in Tel Aviv, then-Prime Minister Yitzhak Shamir and other leaders greeted the new immigrants.

claims.text: מזרחי סיפר שכשהעולים נחתו בישראל הם מיד נישקו את האדמה.
claims.quote: And when they landed in Israel, they immediately kissed the ground

claims.text: לפי Jewish Press, עם ההגעה 140 נוסעים חלשים קיבלו טיפול רפואי עוד על המסלול.
claims.quote: Upon arrival 140 frail passengers received medical care while still on the tarmac

claims.text: לפי JNS וגורמים שהיו מעורבים, מבצע שלמה היה עד אז מבצע העלייה הגדול והמורכב ביותר.
claims.quote: it was also the largest and most complex aliyah mission to date, according to those involved.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, המבצע נערך בסתר, ומאז הוגדר הצלחה הומניטרית גדולה.
claims.quote: This mission was carried out in secret to avoid further complications from the ongoing problems in the area, and has since been deemed a major humanitarian success.

claims.text: מנכ"לית הסוכנות היהודית אמירה אהרונוביץ' אמרה ב-2021, ביובל השלושים למבצע, שהוא מזכיר שכל עם ישראל ערבים זה לזה.
claims.quote: This milestone anniversary of Operation Solomon serves as a crucial reminder for Israel and global Jewry that all of the Jewish people are responsible for one another.

claims.text: לפי ישראל היום ב-2021, במשך יותר מ-40 שנה סייעו הסוכנות היהודית וממשלת ישראל ליותר מ-95,000 יהודי אתיופיה לעלות לישראל.
claims.quote: For more than 40 years, the Jewish Agency and the Israeli government have assisted over 95,000 Ethiopian Jews to move to Israel.

claims.text: לפי JNS, כשלושים שנה אחרי המבצע רחלי תדסה מלכאי, שעלתה בו בגיל 8, מנהלת עמותה שמעצימה נשים אתיופיות.
claims.quote: Today, Racheli Tadesa Malkai runs a successful nonprofit organization that encourages and empowers Ethiopian women to become independent and self-sufficient in their personal and professional lives.

claims.text: לפי JNS, עם הגעתה לישראל התבקשה מלכאי להחליף את שמה האתיופי, אמבת, בשם שבו היא נקראת היום.
claims.quote: upon arriving in Israel, she was asked to change the Ethiopian name her parents gave her, Amevet, to the one she goes by today.

claims.text: מלכאי סיפרה ל-JNS שלדור המבוגר היה קשה יותר להסתגל לחיים בישראל.
claims.quote: The older generation had more of a difficult time acclimating to life in Israel.

claims.text: לפי Jewish Press, המבצע הציל 14,500 יהודי אתיופיה ב-24 וב-25 במאי.
claims.quote: It seemed impossible at the time, but Operation Solomon rescued 14,500 Ethiopian Jews on May 24 and May 25

claims.text: לפי Israel National News, במבצע שנערך ב-24 במאי 1991 הועלו 14,500 יהודי אתיופיה ב-34 מטוסים בתוך 36 שעות.
claims.quote: saw 14,500 Ethiopian Jews airlifted to Israel by 34 planes in 36 hours

claims.text: לפי הקריה האקדמית אונו, אחד המטוסים נשא 1,008 בני אדם, שיא עולמי שלא נשבר למספר הנוסעים הגדול ביותר בטיסה אחת.
claims.quote: One of these aircraft carried 1,008 people – an unbroken world record for the most passengers on a single flight.

claims.text: לפי ה-Jewish Chronicle, עד שבעה תינוקות נולדו במהלך הטיסות.
claims.quote: Mmore people came off the planes than on, as up to seven babies were born during the flights.

claims.text: אבי מזרחי אמר בראיון ב-2021 ששוב יותר מ-14,000 יהודי אתיופיה הגיעו לישראל בתוך 24 שעות.
claims.quote: More than 14,000 Ethiopian Jews were spared from decades of waiting, arriving in Israel via air shuttles within 24 hours
